note: The versions every compatibility claim about zou is made against.
One file, because a claim about PostgREST behaviour is only a claim about
a version of PostgREST, and because the answer to 'compatible with what?'
should be one place rather than a grep.
Everything except supabase-js comes from the image list the supabase CLI
builds its local stack from, which is what 'supabase start' gives people:
apps/cli-go/pkg/config/templates/Dockerfile in github.com/supabase/cli.
supabase-js has no image, so it is the latest 2.x on npm.
Bumping anything here means re-recording the suites it covers, and the
re-recording is the point: a diff under suites/ is upstream
changing its mind, and it should be read rather than merged.
No binary line, because there is no binary. storage-api is published as
an image and nothing else, so the only way to ask it anything is to bring
up the stack, which is what the record workflow in tamnd/zou does. That is
also why the storage suite is checked against its recording in CI and never
diffed against a live reference the way the other three are.
The reference leg of the three realtime suites. Nothing is recorded
from it in the way the auth and rest suites are recorded, but it is
asked: the questions in those suites are ours, and what makes them a
statement about Supabase rather than about zou is that this server
answers them the same way. js-realtime-changes carries a frames.json
besides, which is a recording of this server's frames and is checked
against it in the same run.
It had no line here until the suites were re-pinned and somebody
noticed the reference was moving on its own.
What runs a function in the local stack, and what the functions suite is
diffed against. Nothing is recorded from it: the suite asks both servers
the same questions in the same CI run and each answer is the other's
expected one, which is what the tus and realtime suites do as well.
The corpus, which is a commit rather than a version because it is not
released. It is not vendored here either: examples/corpus.sh brings it
back, and examples/measured.json is what both servers did with it.
Moving this line means re-running the probe against both servers, and
the numbers in examples/README.md move with it.
realtime-js has no line of its own because it has no release of its own.
It lives at packages/core/realtime-js in github.com/supabase/supabase-js and
goes out with it, so the version above is the version of the client the
realtime suite drives.
The same version as supabase-js because it is the same release.
storage-js lives at packages/core/storage-js in github.com/supabase/supabase-js
and goes out with it, so there is nothing here to bump on its own.
The client Supabase's own documentation tells people to use for resumable
uploads, at the latest 4.x on npm. It has no image and no place in the CLI's
list, because it runs in whatever is doing the uploading rather than in the
stack, which is why the suite it covers is the one that drives it.
The one line where zou is deliberately ahead. supabase's local stack is
on 17, zou vendors 18, and a suite that depends on the difference is a
suite that is testing postgres rather than the api in front of it.
